walkthrough:
Combine the fractions over a common denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{(\tan\theta + 1)(1 - \cos\theta) + (\tan\theta - 1)(1 + \cos\theta)}{(1 + \cos\theta)(1 - \cos\theta)}$$

Expand the terms in the numerator:
$$\text{Numerator} = (\tan\theta - \tan\theta\cos\theta + 1 - \cos\theta) + (\tan\theta + \tan\theta\cos\theta - 1 - \cos\theta)$$
$$= 2\tan\theta - 2\cos\theta = 2(\tan\theta - \cos\theta)$$

Set the numerator equal to zero:
$$2(\tan\theta - \cos\theta) = 0 \implies \tan\theta = \cos\theta$$

Use $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$ to obtain a quadratic in $\sin\theta$:
$$\sin\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta \implies \sin^2\theta + \sin\theta - 1 = 0$$

Solve using the quadratic formula for $0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 4(1)(-1)}}{2} = \frac{-1 + \sqrt{5}}{2} \approx 0.618034$$
$$\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.618034) \approx 38.17^\circ \approx 38.2^\circ \quad (\text{to 1 d.p.})$$
